findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] app/models/optimized_image.rb:146-153 — `def self.downsize` is defined twice; Ruby silently keeps only the last definition, so the `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` version is dead code and every existing caller passing width/height positionally (e.g., thumbnail generation in `create_for`) now binds `width` to `dimensions` and `height` to `opts`, raising ArgumentError/TypeError and breaking optimized image generation.

[High/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as both ImageMagick input and output; `convert` does not support in-place conversion (documented to yield blank/truncated output), so the uploaded file can be corrupted instead of resized. It should convert to a temp file and then replace the original.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — the client-side limit is hardcoded to 10MB, replacing the `max_' + type + '_size_kb` lookup; attachments are no longer validated against `max_attachment_size_kb` in the client and will pass the client check only to be rejected by the server.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — the 413 handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit in the 'file too large' message instead of the actual configured `max_image_size_kb`, showing users an incorrect allowed size whenever the setting differs.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — the 5×80% loop cannot guarantee convergence: five passes reduce linear dimensions by at most ~67%, and file size does not scale linearly with dimensions, so a sufficiently oversized image still exceeds `max_image_size_kb` when handed to `Upload.create_for` and fails with a generic error anyway.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`convert_with` is ignored; if `convert` fails (nonzero exit), the loop blindly retries and the possibly corrupted or zero-byte file is still passed to `Upload.create_for`.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `allow_animation` is dead at this call site: `optimize` only selects the animated instructions when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but uploaded tempfiles (Rack multipart paths and `FileHelper.download` paths) have no extension, so animated GIFs are always processed with the static instructions and lose their animation — and the decision is tied to `allow_animated_thumbnails`, a thumbnail setting, rather than the original upload.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — the download cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; admins who configure a limit above 10MB can no longer URL-upload such images, and admins configured below 10MB silently get a larger cap.

[Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:62 — for URL-based uploads, `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` can lack an extension (e.g., `https://host/image?id=1`), so `FileHelper.is_image?` returns false and downsizing is skipped, causing large remote images to fail instead of being resized.

[Low/performance] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — up to five sequential ImageMagick invocations run per oversized upload inside the request cycle, and each pass re-encodes the image, compounding JPEG generation loss; computing a single resize from the target size would be cheaper and degrade quality less.

[Medium/test_gap] no tests were added for the new controller downsizing behavior, and no specs were updated for the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures; existing specs calling `downsize` with width/height would fail and would have caught the duplicate method definition.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as both ImageMagick input and output; `convert` does not support in-place conversion (documented to yield blank/truncated output), so the uploaded file can be corrupted instead of resized. adjudication.rationale: The new upload-resize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e., the same file path is used for both input (`from`) and output (`to`). In `OptimizedImage.convert_with`, the command is executed with `to` as the output path, so this becomes an in-place rewrite. Many image conversion pipelines (and commonly ImageMagick `convert`) are unsafe when input and output are the same file, risking truncation/corruption of the uploaded file during the downsizing attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — the 413 handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit in the 'file too large' message instead of the actual configured `max_image_size_kb`, showing users an incorrect allowed size whenever the setting differs.

adjudication.rationale: In the 413 handler in `utilities.js`, the diff replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the “file too large” alert will report 10MB regardless of the actual configured `max_image_size_kb`, so users can be shown an incorrect allowed size when the setting differs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — the 5×80% loop cannot guarantee convergence: five passes reduce linear dimensions by at most ~67%, and file size does not scale linearly with dimensions, so a sufficiently oversized image still exceeds `max_image_size_kb` when handed to `Upload.create_for` and fails with a generic error anyway.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a best-effort downsizing loop in `create_upload` that runs at most 5 iterations and stops even if `tempfile.size` remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (uploads_controller.rb: new while loop). From the diff alone, it’s true this cannot guarantee the image will end up under the limit; if it remains oversized, the code still calls `Upload.create_for(...)` with the (still too-large) `tempfile.size`, so the upload may be rejected downstream. However, this is not a clear correctness regression introduced by the change—previously oversized uploads would be rejected outright—so it’s better framed as an incomplete/edge-case issue rather than a definite bug. The claim about a “generic error” cannot be verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`convert_with` is ignored; if `convert` fails (nonzero exit), the loop blindly retries and the possibly corrupted or zero-byte file is still passed to `Upload.create_for`.

adjudication.rationale: In the new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb`, `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` is called without checking its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` when the underlying `convert` command fails (nonzero exit), and no exception is raised. From the diff alone we can verify the failure signal is ignored; however, whether this results in a corrupted/zero-byte file being passed to `Upload.create_for` (or whether later validations reject it) is not shown in the diff, so the worst-case behavior is plausible but not strictly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `allow_animation` is dead at this call site: `optimize` only selects the animated instructions when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but uploaded tempfiles (Rack multipart paths and `FileHelper.download` paths) have no extension, so animated GIFs are always processed with the static instructions and lose their animation — and the decision is tied to `allow_animated_thumbnails`, a thumbnail setting, rather than the original upload.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated instruction path is only selected when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is the tempfile path (from Rack multipart tempfiles or `FileHelper.download`), which the diff shows is created without any `.gif`-based naming (e.g. `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`), so the regex check is likely to fail even for GIF uploads. That makes `allow_animation` effectively inert at this call site and can cause animated GIFs to be processed using the non-animated instructions during downsizing, potentially losing animation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — the download cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; admins who configure a limit above 10MB can no longer URL-upload such images, and admins configured below 10MB silently get a larger cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the URL-download size limit in `UploadsController#create_upload` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This makes the cap ignore admin configuration: settings >10MB will be rejected for URL uploads, and settings <10MB will allow downloading up to 10MB before later downsizing logic runs. This behavior change is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:62 — for URL-based uploads, `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` can lack an extension (e.g., `https://host/image?id=1`), so `FileHelper.is_image?` returns false and downsizing is skipped, causing large remote images to fail instead of being resized.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_upload`, URL-based uploads set `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`. If the URL path has no extension (e.g. `/image` or empty because the real name is in query params), the new downsizing block `... && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` will evaluate false and skip resizing even when `tempfile` is an actual oversized image. Since the intent of the added block is to allow oversized images to be reduced before `Upload.create_for(...)`, this can cause large remote images to still be rejected instead of downsized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-68 — up to five sequential ImageMagick invocations run per oversized upload inside the request cycle, and each pass re-encodes the image, compounding JPEG generation loss; computing a single resize from the target size would be cheaper and degrade quality less.

adjudication.rationale: The added loop in `uploads_controller.rb` can run up to 5 times per upload (`attempt = 5` with `while ... tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`), calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` each iteration. Given `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately runs ImageMagick via `convert_with` (backticks), this is multiple sequential re-encodes during the request, which is a concrete performance/quality concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] no tests were added for the new controller downsizing behavior, and no specs were updated for the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures; existing specs calling `downsize` with width/height would fail and would have caught the duplicate method definition.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb` the diff introduces two `self.downsize` definitions back-to-back: one with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and later another with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the latter overwrites the former, so any existing callers passing 4 args (width/height) will raise `ArgumentError`, and the first wrapper is effectively dead code. This is a concrete behavioral break introduced by the diff; the finding’s point that tests weren’t updated to catch this aligns with the risk.
